must_remember: A streamline is an imaginary curve whose tangent at any point indicates the direction of the fluid velocity vector.
Two streamlines can never intersect, as an intersection would imply two different velocity vectors at a single spatial point.
The Equation of Continuity $A_1 v_1 = A_2 v_2$ is based on the conservation of mass for an incompressible fluid.
Reynolds number $R_e = \frac{\rho v d}{\eta}$ determines the transition from streamlined to turbulent flow; critical value for pipes is roughly 2000.
In irrotational flow, fluid elements possess no net angular velocity about their center of mass ($\omega = 0$), allowing the use of velocity potential $\phi$.

glossary.meaning: An imaginary curve drawn in a fluid showing the instantaneous direction of fluid velocity.
Statement of mass conservation for steady incompressible flow: $A v = \text{constant}$.
A dimensionless number used to predict flow transition from laminar/streamlined to turbulent.
A scalar function whose negative gradient yields the velocity vector in irrotational flows.
A scalar function used in 2D incompressible flow where lines of constant $\psi$ represent streamlines.
